f05d1524424f5ec5484b5d0858fee86919307ec0.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence report (published 2024-05-28) on Moonstone Sleet, a threat actor Microsoft assesses is North Korean state-aligned and formerly tracked as Storm-1789. It links the actor to Diamond Sleet and describes fake companies and job lures, trojanized PuTTY loaders (SplitLoader, YouieLoad), a malicious tank game called DeTankWar, malicious npm packages, and the FakePenny ransomware, which demanded $6.6M USD in BTC. Targets named include software, education and defense industrial base organisations. Microsoft assesses the actor's aims as espionage and revenue generation.

hedges: Microsoft assesses the actor is North Korean state-aligned; this is the report's assessment, not a confirmed attribution.
Microsoft assesses the ransomware objective is financial gain, suggesting the actor runs operations for both intelligence collection and revenue.
Microsoft assesses the actor has capabilities from prior North Korean cyber operations, because its early attacks reused Diamond Sleet methods and code.
The purpose of the fake-company relationships is unclear; they may give access to organisations or be used for revenue.
The IT-worker activity could be consistent with earlier US Department of Justice reporting, or may be another way to gain access to organisations.
The report says Onyx Sleet involvement 'may suggest' the actor is expanding into disruptive operations.
Microsoft has not yet identified any Moonstone Sleet supply chain attacks.
Shared use of npm packages across North Korean groups may suggest sharing of expertise and TTPs.
